_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.the_false_constraint_caught_before_it_wa: TLT's 84C costs $59.50. XLP, XLF, XLU and XLE trade at $43-86 spot. The natural inference -- and the one this run was on the point of recording as a structural exclusion -- is that these names cannot produce a $300-1,000 TACTICAL or $500-1,000 CORE position and are therefore out of reach, a tidy mirror of the documented 'AMD is priced out' tier finding.
_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.why_it_is_wrong_measured_not_modelled: Spread as a percentage of mid is a PER-CONTRACT property, entirely independent of quantity. TEN TLT 2026-09-18 84C = $595.00, dead centre of the CORE band, at 1.68% of mid, delta 0.415, OI 51,155, with a 546 x 784 book that absorbs the size without strain. Every ratio the gates actually test -- spread %, delta, OI, DTE, premium at risk -- is identical or better than a single-contract position on a pricier name.
_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.what_it_opens: The liquid low-priced ETF universe (TLT, XLP, XLF, XLU, XLE and peers) is available to BOTH tracks and has never been hunted. It matters most on exactly the days that keep stalling this desk: when index and mega-cap boards are blocked by one single-name earnings print, these instruments are uncorrelated with it and quote far tighter than the equity report's mid-cap screen -- 1.68% of mid today against that screen's 12.6-52%.
_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.the_honest_limits: Three, so no future run over-reads this. (1) It supplies NO thesis -- this run measured the chain and still declined the trade. (2) Per-contract commissions scale with quantity where they apply, so a 10-lot pays ten times any per-contract fee even though the spread ratio is unchanged; check the fee line in review_option_order before sizing large lots. (3) Depth must be verified at the intended size, not assumed from OI -- 51,155 OI with a 546 x 784 top-of-book is fine for a 10-lot and would not be for a 500-lot.
_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.the_transferable_lesson: This is the FOURTH instance of this file's oldest bug and the FIRST caught before being written down rather than after. Spot price (2026-08-14), ATM strike (2026-08-17), wrong expiry board (2026-08-24), and now quantity-of-one. Each time a name was declared untradeable from a quote that was never the test. The fix never changes: QUOTE IT. And note the asymmetry that makes this one worth keeping -- the previous three instances wrongly EXCLUDED tradeable names, and so did this one; the bug has never once erred toward taking a bad trade, which is precisely why it survives so long unnoticed.

_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.subject: THE CONCURRENT-RUN COLLISION FINALLY HAPPENED ON THE EQUITY BOOK, AND IT BREACHED THE CASH FLOOR BY AN AMOUNT NEITHER RUN COULD HAVE SEEN. The mitigation CLAUDE.md prescribes -- re-fetch origin/master before placing -- WAS PERFORMED, CORRECTLY, AND DID NOT WORK. Measured 2026-08-28T13:50Z.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.what_happened: Two scheduler-fired runs executed the same first-post-open slot: session ...OfEc (fired 13:30:28Z) and session ...1TG2 (fired 13:38Z). Each read the same committed report, each ran the full v8 gate stack, each graded the screen independently, and each took its own 1-of-1 per-run equity entry. ...OfEc bought ROST 2 sh @ 230.1512 = $460.30, filled 13:37:13Z. ...1TG2 bought MDLZ 7.988509 sh @ 62.59 = $500.00, filled ~13:40Z. Both entries are individually sound and both survive review on their merits -- this is NOT a case of a bad trade.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.the_arithmetic_that_matters: EACH RUN'S SIZING WAS COMPLIANT ALONE; THE PAIR IS NOT. Pre-trade the equity book was cash $2,507.26 / equity $939.45, so the posture's max compliant buy was 2507.26 - 0.45 x 3446.71 = $956.24 -- and $460.30 and $500.00 each sit comfortably under it. Together they are $960.30, which is $4.06 OVER. Measured live at 13:47Z: cash $1,546.96, equity_value $1,892.33, book $3,439.29, floor reading 44.98% against the >=45% Aug-Oct minimum. On cost rather than marks it is 44.88%. The breach is real and it is small -- roughly $4 of a $3,440 book, 0.12pp.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.why_the_prescribed_mitigation_failed_and: CLAUDE.md says: 'BEFORE any place order, re-fetch origin/master and re-read holdings.json + trade_journal.json. If a sibling entry has landed since this run began, DEFER.' ...OfEc performed exactly that at 13:36:59Z and master was clean at cda3f4e. It WAS clean -- the sibling had not yet committed. THE LEDGER LAGS A SIBLING'S FILL BY THAT SIBLING'S COMMIT LATENCY, which here was about 2.5 minutes (ROST filled 13:37:13Z, the commit recording it landed ~13:47Z). A git-based check therefore has a blind window exactly as long as the other run's write-up, and a run that researches carefully before committing is a run whose fill is invisible for LONGER. The check is not merely imperfect; it is systematically blind in the direction that matters.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.THE_FIX: RE-READ THE BROKER, NOT ONLY origin/master, IMMEDIATELY BEFORE ANY ORDER: get_equity_positions and get_portfolio for equities, get_option_positions for options. The broker reflects a sibling's fill in the same second; the repository reflects it minutes later. Then recompute the gate off THOSE numbers rather than off the numbers read at run start. PROVEN ON THIS EXACT INCIDENT: had ...1TG2 re-read the broker at ~13:39Z it would have seen ROST already held, giving cash $2,046.96 / equity ~$1,399.75 and a max compliant buy of 2046.96 - 0.45 x 3446.71 = $495.94. Its $500.00 order was $4.06 over that -- so a broker re-read would have caught this breach precisely, and a $495 order would have been fully compliant. The fix is not theoretical; it closes THIS hole exactly.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.second_order_lesson: A pre-trade gate computed at RUN START is stale by the time the order is sent, even with no sibling involved -- marks move. The cash floor in particular is defined as a function of live cash and live equity value, so it must be recomputed from a fresh get_portfolio at order time. 'I checked the floor this run' is not the same claim as 'the floor holds at the moment I am sending this order'.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.what_was_NOT_done_and_why: NEITHER POSITION WAS UNWOUND TO CURE THE BREACH. Restoring 45% requires raising about $4 of cash; selling a $4 sliver of a position pays a spread and a round trip to correct a rounding-scale overshoot, and the floor is written as a SIZING gate ('compute it BEFORE proposing a size', 'max compliant buy = ...'), not as a continuous constraint that forces liquidation -- ordinary mark drift moves this reading across 45% daily in either direction. The correct response is to STOP ADDING, which is what has been done: the equity book is closed to further entries today until the floor reads >=45% again. Reported to Ryan the same session rather than buried in a ledger key.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.MDLZ_LEDGER_OWNERSHIP: RESOLVED at the final merge: the sibling committed MDLZ to positions[] in PR #790 (7.988509 sh @ 62.5899, order 6a918fb3), so the ledger now carries all four equity positions and matches the broker one-for-one. The earlier concern -- that writing the position from this side would duplicate it -- was correct and the deliberate omission was the right call; the sibling's own record landed intact.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.cross_reference: Precedent: the 2026-08-13 collision (13:00Z/13:10Z and 17:02Z/17:05Z pairs) which cost nothing because both runs declined. CLAUDE.md predicted this exact escalation -- 'two concurrent runs finding the same A-grade setup would BOTH place it' -- and the only thing it got wrong is that they found DIFFERENT setups, so the breach came through the shared cash floor rather than through a doubled position.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.only_ryan_can_fix_the_root: The redundant trigger configuration (cron-job.org sub-hourly + the routine's native hourly backstop) is what puts two runs in one slot, and it is Ryan's to change. An agent can only make each collision harmless. This key is the in-repo defence until then.
